entries.key: The Hedgehog was a forward-throwing anti-submarine weapon used during the Battle of the Atlantic. Developed by the British Royal Navy, it fired up to 24 spigot mortars ahead of a ship when attacking a U-boat. It was deployed on convoy escort warships to supplement the depth charges. As the mortar projectiles employed contact fuzes rather than time or barometric (depth) fuzes, detonation occurred directly against a hard surface such as a submarine hull making it more deadly than depth charges.<cr>On May 11 1943, Convoy SC 130, comprising 37 ships, left Nova Scotia bound for North West England. Ranged against the convoy were 25 U-boats in three patrol lines. Several of the U-boats engaged the convoy and its escorts. British long-range aircraft also attacked the U-boats.<cr>During the action on May 19th and 20th, U-954 was sunk by hedgehog attacks from warships HMS Sennen and HMS Jed. German Admiral Karl Doenitz's son Peter Doenitz was among those lost aboard U-954.<cr>No convoy ships were lost. 3 U-boats were sunk and 4 more were damaged. This was a major blow which contributed to Admiral Doenitz's decision to abandon the assault on the North Atlantic convoy route, a turning point in the Battle of the Atlantic.<cr>Note Picture: Hedgehog attack against U-853 in 1945.
